mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and economic growth, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a UNRATE decline, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) suggests increased demand in the housing market, which may lead to broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts do not precede positive S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over 60 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.15% indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate investment and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following a FEDFUNDS drop below 0.15%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and decreases in UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) at an annualized rate above 2% indicates strong economic growth, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If real GDP growth above 2% does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) at an annualized rate above 5% indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If retail sales growth above 5% does not precede positive S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over 20 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) may indicate a specific monetary policy stance, which could influence equity valuations and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following the specified combination of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is falsified.
